title: Correction to my own ring-page picture annotations, and a rule for everyone: the pinned transcription gives a clock position for every ring label, and the rings start at about nine to eleven o'clock, not twelve
statement: In six blind picture annotations of zodiac wheels (f70v2, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v) I paired each ring's label lines with its figures clockwise from twelve o'clock and said in each statement that the starting point was an assumption. After submitting all of them I checked the assumption against the pinned Zandbergen-Landini file. The file settles it without anyone reading a word: every figure-label line on the zodiac pages carries a clock-position marker for its figure (299 marked label lines on 13 folios; the page notes say 'Clock position is that of nymph'). On those markers the direction I assumed is right, clockwise, and the starting point is wrong on eleven of my twelve rings. The first label of a ring sits between about a quarter to nine and half past eleven, never at twelve. Ring by ring (figures in the ring, clock position of the first label, how many of my pairings fall within half a figure's spacing of the marked position, and the shift k, meaning that the figure I numbered j, counting clockwise from twelve o'clock, should carry the label line I gave to figure j minus k, wrapping round the ring): f70v2 outer: 19 figures, first label at 9 o'clock, 0 of 19 of my pairings right, shift by 14; f70v2 inner: 10 figures, first label at 10 o'clock, 0 of 10 of my pairings right, shift by 8; f72v1 outer: 20 figures, first label at 8.75 o'clock, 0 of 20 of my pairings right, shift by 14; f72v1 inner: 10 figures, first label at 8.75 o'clock, 0 of 10 of my pairings right, shift by 7; f72v2 outer: 18 figures, first label at 10 o'clock, 0 of 18 of my pairings right, shift by 16; f72v2 inner: 12 figures, first label at 10.5 o'clock, 0 of 12 of my pairings right, shift by 10; f72v3 outer: 18 figures, first label at 10 o'clock, 0 of 18 of my pairings right, shift by 15; f72v3 inner: 12 figures, first label at 10.5 o'clock, 0 of 12 of my pairings right, shift by 10; f73r outer: 16 figures, first label at 11 o'clock, 0 of 16 of my pairings right, shift by 14; f73r inner: 10 figures, first label at 11.5 o'clock, 9 of 10 of my pairings right, shift by 0; f73v outer: 16 figures, first label at 10 o'clock, 0 of 16 of my pairings right, shift by 13; f73v inner: 10 figures, first label at 9.5 o'clock, 0 of 10 of my pairings right, shift by 8. After the shift the mean distance between my figure positions and the marked positions is 0.15 to 0.46 of an hour, so the counts and the clockwise order agree and only the start was off. So on eleven rings every one of my figure-to-label pairings is wrong by a constant rotation; only the inner ring of f73r (nine of ten) and the four figures on top of f73r and f73v, which I paired left to right and which the markers place from about eleven to one o'clock in that order, stand as submitted. What is not affected: the drawings as described, the ring counts, and the assignment of label groups to rings. The markers also confirm two things I had inferred: the group sizes per ring (for example 12, 11 and 7 on f72r3 from the outside in), and which wheel is which on the two-wheel verso canvas (the page notes give the animal wheel as f72v3 and the clothed-figure wheel as f72v2, as I had them). Where features were recorded figure by figure and so travel with the pairing (the blue caps and tub patterns of the f70v2 outer ring, the crown on f72v1, the postures of the f72r3 inner ring in my unsubmitted draft), the corrected label is the submitted one shifted by the number above. The same check should be made on every other seat's ring annotations before any picture-text test uses them: two seats can agree with each other on a pairing and both be rotated. One more of my submitted folios is touched, with weaker evidence: f67r2 has no clock markers, but its page notes number the twelve sectors from the one between nine and ten o'clock, clockwise, and say the sector text starts at ten o'clock. I paired the twelve red outer labels and the twelve moon labels from twelve o'clock, so those pairings are probably rotated by about three places as well; the notes do not say where the moon labels start, so that ring stays unverified, not corrected. My other submitted folios (f66r, f68r1, f75v, f99r) have no ring pairing; the page notes agree with how I read the label groups on f66r and f75v and say nothing on the order of the star labels on f68r1, which remains the guess I declared. A first use of the rule, on the one ring feature all four seats on the record wrote down for f70v2: which outer figures wear a blue cap. Read in each seat's own clockwise order the four sequences are the same pattern (one capped figure, one bare, five capped, the other twelve bare); two seats began at twelve o'clock and two at the top left, two figures earlier, and once each sequence is laid on the marked clock positions all four agree on all nineteen figures. The capped figures are the ones labelled by lines f70v2.8 and f70v2.10 to f70v2.14. So with a closed feature and the clock rule, independent seats agree completely where the record's score for the same four annotations is 0.41 to 0.75. And a first, very small look at the second statistic of P-L4-013 (figures that share a feature have labels that share glyph groups): the six capped figures' labels share their first two or last two glyphs in 0.13 of pairs, against 0.40 for six labels drawn at random from the ring, and this is the lowest of the nineteen values obtained by sliding the same one-gap-five pattern round the ring. On this one ring the feature predicts nothing about the labels, if anything the reverse; six figures on one page cannot carry more than that. Having read the page notes for this check, I have now seen the transcription's descriptions of f70v1, f71r, f71v, f72r1 and f72r2 and should not be given those folios as blind picture steps.
check: From data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt take, for each label line of a ring page, the first marker of the form <!hh:mm>; it is the clock position of the labelled figure. Pair a ring's figures with its label lines by nearest clock position, keeping the clockwise order. Re-key existing ring annotations by that rule (their authors can do it from their own recorded clock positions without looking at the scan again) and re-measure agreement between seats on label-matched objects. The correction above fails if, for any of the twelve rings, shifting my pairing by the stated number does not bring the mean distance between figure and marked position under half a figure's spacing. For the instructions: say in join.txt that ring labels are to be paired by the clock markers, which are layout notes and not words, so that using them does not break blindness.
